title: Bonded-summon presence transition leaves a participant-turn clock anchored to the departed combatant (begin_turn/close_combat_instance then refuse)
description:
DEFECT CLASS (state integrity, reachable): a participant-turn clock whose participant leaves play or changes identity during a bonded-summon presence transition. transition_bonded_summon rebinds the leaving combatant's target/link/source-actor references to its campaign_actor, but the clock's anchor_participant_kind/ref still name the combatant. The committed row then violates the participant-timer invariant, and every later validation of that combat's timers refuses.

## Steps to Reproduce
Static trace (confirmed by Claude Captain against main f7d70b64, packages/core/src/state/activeEffects.ts):
1. start_effect accepts a timed round duration anchored 'target-turn-start' to a single combatant target (toolEffectShared.ts anchor enum).
2. A bonded familiar/steed combatant can be that sole target.
3. transitionBondedSummon (~l.5703) for every non-recall trigger (action-temporary-dismissal -> pocketed; action-permanent-dismissal, action-dismissal, action-release -> absent) calls rebindCombatantReferencesToActor (~l.6564), which rewrites active_effect_target combatant->campaign_actor (and links, and source_actor) but never touches anchor_participant_*.
4. requireParticipantTimerDeadline (~l.1129) requires a target-turn-start anchor to equal the effect's sole target -> now mismatched.
5. settleEffectsAtTurnBoundary (~l.6408) validates EVERY participant timer anchored to the combat instance before any settlement, so the next begin_turn throws and rolls back: the combat cannot advance.
6. Sibling consequence: combat closure (~l.6725) runs the same pre-validation, so close_combat_instance also refuses.
Sibling to check (include only if reachable by a legitimate tool sequence): a 'source-turn-start' clock whose source actor is the departing combatant — the source_actor rebind produces the same anchor/source mismatch.

DESIGN REQUIREMENT: choose a bounded, source-justified disposition for a participant-turn clock whose participant leaves play (settle/expire at the transition, or another SRD-justified behavior) and apply it inside the transition transaction with ledger evidence. Mechanically rebinding the anchor to campaign_actor is NOT acceptable: a campaign actor is not a turn participant and the clock could never advance. Decide explicitly what temporary dismissal (pocket) followed by action-recall means for the clock (recall enters as a NEW combatant identity).
History: eshyra-82uk.1 deliberately left participant-turn clocks and concentration out of the rebind, deferring this decision here.
design: 2026-10-08 Claude Captain (supersedes the earlier design text). DISPOSITION: expire. Inside transitionBondedSummon, for the departing kinds (pocket, dismiss, release) and BEFORE rebindCombatantReferencesToActor, every live (active/suppressed) participant-turn timer (target-turn-start OR source-turn-start) anchored in this instance to the departing combatant ends with reason 'expired' via finalizeEnd; reported as result.timersExpired and in the presence-transition event. RATIONALE: participant clocks are combatant-only by contract (closure rebind comment); the transition rebinds the effect's target/source to campaign_actor, which is not a turn participant, and a recall enters as a NEW combatant identity, so the clock can no longer describe the creature in play. Mechanically rebinding the anchor is invalid; keeping target+anchor on the absent row (as the 0-HP vanish path does, which never rebinds) would split the effect's references and leave it on a stale row after recall. Closure precedent: round-scale timers whose clock leaves expire. NOTE: begin_turn does still establish boundaries for absent participants, so the justification is identity, not 'the clock can never tick'. If the bond effect itself carries such a clock, the transition refuses (fail closed). Source-turn-start sibling is reachable (start_effect accepts a combatant source actor) and is included.
acceptance_criteria:
- Permanent regression via a legitimate model-tool sequence: start_effect with a target-turn-start clock on a bonded familiar/steed combatant -> transition_bonded_summon dismissal -> begin_turn advances (and close_combat_instance closes) without refusal.
- The test distinguishes the invalid retained clock (must not survive) from a valid surviving or settled effect (asserts the chosen disposition and its ledger evidence).
- Sibling triggers (pocket/temporary dismissal, permanent dismissal, dismissal, release) covered where the same invariant applies; source-turn-start sibling covered only if reachable.
- No mechanical rebinding of a participant-turn anchor to campaign_actor.
notes:
2026-10-08 (Claude Captain): raised P4->P2 and retyped bug after confirming audit result C against main f7d70b64 — the sequence is reachable through ordinary model tools and blocks turn advancement and combat closure. Previous description (dismissal 'would keep referencing the now-absent row; decide whether dismissal should settle') superseded by the full defect class above.

Implemented inline by Claude Captain: expireDepartingParticipantTimers in transitionBondedSummon; timersExpired in result/event/tool description; 5 regression tests in bondedSummonTransitions.test.ts with negative proof (pre-fix begin_turn refuses with the anchor/target mismatch). Bond self-clock branch dropped: unreachable (start_effect forces bonded-summon effects to until-removed). verify:worktree green (6044 passed / 3 skipped). Stays in_progress until merge.
